what_its_for: This medicine is used to lower very high levels of triglycerides (a type of fat) in your blood. High triglycerides can increase your risk of serious health problems, including pancreatitis (a painful inflammation of the pancreas). Your doctor has prescribed this medication because your triglyceride levels are very high (500 mg/dL or above).
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with or without food. Swallow the capsules whole — do not crush, chew, or break them open. Take it exactly as your doctor prescribed. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. This medicine works best when combined with a healthy low-fat diet and regular exercise.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 4 grams (4 capsules) per day. Your doctor may tell you to take all 4 capsules at one time, or to take 2 capsules in the morning and 2 capsules in the evening. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused or expired capsules.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating high-fat or high-cholesterol foods while taking this medicine, as they can make it less effective. Limit or avoid alcohol, since alcohol can raise your triglyceride levels. Tell your doctor if you are taking blood thinners (such as warfarin/Coumadin), as omega-3-acid ethyl esters may increase your risk of bleeding. Avoid taking this medicine if you are allergic to fish or shellfish without first talking to your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: unusual or easy bruising or bleeding; severe stomach or back pain (which could be a sign of pancreatitis); chest pain or irregular heartbeat; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, itching, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); or if your symptoms do not improve after several weeks of treatment. Also tell your doctor about all other medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking.
when_it_works: You may not feel any different while taking this medicine because high triglycerides usually do not cause obvious symptoms. Your doctor will check your triglyceride levels with a blood test after about 4 to 8 weeks to see how well the medicine is working. It is important to keep taking it even if you feel fine. Continue eating a healthy diet and exercising regularly to get the best results.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before taking this medicine. The risks and benefits should be discussed with your doctor. Elderly patients: Older adults may use this medicine safely, but should be monitored closely by their doctor. Children: This medicine is generally not approved for use in children. Fish or shellfish allergy: If you are allergic to fish or shellfish, talk to your doctor before taking this medicine, as it is derived from fish oil and may trigger an allergic reaction.
